- User prefers detailed explanation of Figure 4 showing time-frequency diagram of intra-pulse frequency agile echo signal
- User requested re-explanation of Figure 4 for better understanding of time-frequency separation
- Pulse-to-pulse and intra-pulse frequency agile waveforms create frequency differences between target and jamming signals
- Time-domain slicing by sub-pulse width enables effective jamming suppression
- Fractional Fourier transform domain processing with narrowband filters separates target from jamming
- Segmented pulse compression accumulates sub-pulses after jamming suppression
- Random frequency hopping causes jamming residuals to distribute uniformly in range dimension
- Pulse-to-pulse and intra-pulse frequency agile waveforms avoid continuous "bright band" formation in time-frequency domain
